episode.showDescription: Cougar Sports with Ben Criddle (@criddlebenjamin) keeps you up-to-date on all things BYU Sports. We not only cover football & basketball, but we dive into recruiting, baseball, soccer, and more. For insight that you can't get anywhere else, tune into 103.9/ 98.3 FM. Monday-Friday from 2-6 PM MST. Follow us on social media @espnthefan & interact with us using #ESPNTheFan.
episode.episodeDescription: Ben Criddle talks BYU sports every weekday from 2 to 6 pm. transcript_window.text: We caught up with him last year at Big 12 Media Days.
It was a phenomenal interview, a lot of interconnectivity between him and BYU.
Now he's leading the charge at TCU.
Let's welcome in the athletic director for TCU.
Mike, buddy.
Mike, how you living?
I'm living large, Ben.
Living large.
I'm glad I only had to get in my car and drive over here instead of having to get on an airplane like this.
You bro.
You can get a power walk out over here.
It's home field advantage anytime you can get it.
Hey, you'll take it operationally, logistically, administratively.
It's a great day for you and your crew.
So Big 12 Media Days, reconnecting, discussing the vision of TCU athletics.
TCU's in a great spot right now.
There's stability.

um you're you're in your role here uh now how long has it been since you've taken over the role about a year and a half okay so we're a year and a half in how would you evaluate your uh your tenure thus far year and a half how would you break it down yeah you know it's interesting it's really hard to i guess self -assess progress

because college athletics as a whole has been kind of thrown into this madness that we're in so you know coming from a place like west point and get thrown into this blender of moving to Texas, going to a civilian institution in the midst of NIL and above the cap and revenue share,
there's no better place, in my opinion, to be than in Fort Worth and at a place like TCU to deal with all of these challenges.
But let's be clear, these are challenges.

And there's a reason that Congress is involved and there's a reason that Brian Santiago and myself and 14 others in our position are communicating more than ever we share similar frustrations and challenges that we're trying to overcome.

And at the core of what we do, and I would say BYU is one that does it as well as anybody being a faith -based institution, caring about education, caring about developing young people, holding them accountable, developing them from a character standpoint.
Those conversations are being lost and they're too few and far between.
But we still try to make that the main thing.
And it's hard to keep the main thing, the main thing, unless you have really strong leadership continuity.
